scores.evidence: Phase 1 "Containment and gating" ... "Depends on: V1 and V2" (Phase 2); "Resolve capability design | V3 (triage works...)"
scores.rationale: Phases run substrate, defenses, retrieval/triage, resolve, widen, with explicit dependencies and gates proven before dependent work is specified.

scores.evidence: A real issue is opened in a sandbox repo ... webhook ... queue ... worker ... model API ... applies the label and posts a comment
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a real end-to-end deployed slice with deploy, rollback, and observability.

scores.evidence: Hosted model under enterprise terms ... Flip condition: V1 denies: self-hosted or private-endpoint model
scores.rationale: Irreversible decisions are listed with reversibility, default, assumption, validator and flip condition.

scores.evidence: Tasks in order: 1. Freeze the action schema and the tool-executor contract ... 2. rulesets ... 3. Build the sandbox runner
scores.rationale: Within phases, the widest-impact items (executor contract, rulesets) precede leaf items like caps and test suites; Phase 4 widens one repo at a time.

scores.evidence: 0: HMAC verification, least-privilege App, sandbox repo only ... 1: Executor allow-list, bound approvals ... 4: Per-repo install review
scores.rationale: Concrete security treatment appears in every phase starting with Phase 0.

scores.evidence: OpenTelemetry trace per issue across all tiers ... Alerts on dead-letter depth, error rate, and cost-cap hits.
scores.rationale: Observability is concrete in Phase 0 and each later phase.

scores.evidence: Each run records image, model, prompt, and repo commit so it can be replayed
scores.rationale: Pinned images, IaC, pinned model, versioned prompts/index/eval sets, and run replay are threaded through all phases.

scores.evidence: Kill switch, idempotent webhook handling, dead-letter queue, loop guard
scores.rationale: Resilience appears concretely in every phase, from the kill switch in Phase 0 to per-repo kill in Phase 4.

scores.evidence: Phase 1: Containment and gating (defenses before capability) ... retrieval Phase 2, memory/orchestration Phase 3, routing/feedback Phase 4
scores.rationale: Defenses, budgets and human gating precede retrieval, model access, memory, orchestration, routing and feedback, in the right order.

scores.evidence: Auto-merge or auto-approve: pulled forward only if a long record of accepted PRs on a low-risk class exists and security signs off.
scores.rationale: Deferred items are explicit, each with a pull-forward condition.

note: Very strong plan that meets every rubric dimension with concrete content; the only minor quibble is that memory is listed after orchestration-adjacent work in Phase 3.
